newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals led by PGMs dive by limits.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals led by PGMs dive by limits.

text.p: Most yen-based Tokyo precious metals except for gold tumbled by their daily price limits on Wednesday after roller coaster trade, traders said.

Most palladium futures jumped by their 48 yen price limits at the outset, and immediately after the opening heavy long-liquidation by a U.S. trader who was believed to have massive longs in TOCOM unleashed large-lot long positions.

"The volume of the long-liquidation was unusually large. The heavy long-liquidation by the trader triggered selling from other traders. Near-term direction is completely unpredictable," one analyst at a commodity broker said.

It was not clear what was behind the large-scale long-liquidation in palladium, traders said. Benchmark June palladium fell by its 48 yen per gram limit to 707 yen. Benchmark June platinum fell by its 75 yen limit to 1,519 yen.

Another trader said it was highly likely that PGM prices would turn higher again. "Volatile trade in PGMs is expected to continue, given the fact that short positions in TOCOM palladium futures remain," one trading house trader said.
Although traders expected August platinum group metals (PGMs) shipments from Russia to start arriving soon, most of them are expected to go straight to end-users.

TOCOM open interest in platinum and palladium stood at 344,524 lots and 122,593 lots, respectively, as of Tuesday. Platinum futures extended early losses on the heels of palladium, but the physical platinum market was not as tight as that of palladium, traders said.
Spot gold was quoted at $318.85/319.15 per ounce at 0743 GMT, against $320.20/70 in New York on Tuesday.

Gold futures settled lower, pressured by the yen's recovery against the dollar late in the day. Trade was lacklustre with most attention centering on PGMs. Benchmark June ended down nine at 1,209 yen. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk
